articles.title: Can You Get a UFC Title Shot If No One Knows Your Name?
articles.description: New DraftKings Customers turn five bucks into one hundred and fifty in total bonuses, paid over 14 days. The Crown Is Yours! Sign up using https://dkng.co/sonnen or through my promo code SONNEN. #DKPartner Christian Leroy Duncan says a win over Brendan Allen should put him in the UFC middleweight title conversation. Most people will immediately tell him no. Chael Sonnen explains why that reaction may actually mean Duncan is doing exactly the right thing. The middleweight division is unusually unsettled. Khamzat Chimaev has talked about taking time away if the UFC doesn't book him soon, the championship picture remains unclear, and Nassourdine Imavov appears positioned to play a major role in whatever comes next. That creates opportunity. Chael explains why repeatedly associating your name with a title shot matters, even before fans believe you deserve one, and why Duncan could make an even smarter move if he beats Brendan Allen. Instead of asking for the belt, Chael believes CLD should grab the microphone and go directly after Imavov. A personal rivalry is harder to dismiss than another fighter simply asking for a championship opportunity. If Duncan plants that seed now and the middleweight division breaks the right way, he could suddenly find himself much closer to the title than anyone expected. articles.title: Why Strickland Won’t Walk Away #ufc
articles.description: Sean Strickland wants $1 million to fight Nassourdine Imavov — and Imavov reportedly came back with a $500,000 offer of his own, provided he beats Strickland. But Chael Sonnen doesn’t believe fear is what’s keeping this fight from happening. Chael explains why he thinks Strickland is still determined to reclaim the UFC middleweight title. After losing the belt, Strickland made it clear that he believed the championship had been taken from him. In Chael’s view, that motivation hasn’t disappeared. Strickland has already fought Imavov, so the usual accusations about being afraid of an opponent don’t carry much weight. The real question is what happens if the two sides can’t agree on the matchup. Does the UFC find a different opponent? Does the situation become more complicated? And how does the promotion handle a contender who still wants the belt but may not agree to the proposed terms? Chael breaks down the money, the motivation, and the difficult matchmaking decision facing the UFC. #ChaelSonnen #SeanStrickland #NassourdineImavov #UFC #MMA #UFCMiddleweight #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis

articles.title: Michael Bisping’s Pereira Claim Sparks a Bigger Question #ufc
articles.description: Could Alex Pereira be fighting for the final time? Chael Sonnen says he’s now considering something he never thought he would: Pereira losing to Sergei Pavlovich — and potentially walking away from MMA afterward. The conversation starts with Michael Bisping’s claim that Pereira’s flat-footed style could leave him vulnerable to a knockout against the heavyweight striker. Chael acknowledges the risk, but says the bigger question is what happens if Pereira actually loses. At 39, Pereira has already built an extraordinary MMA résumé. But Chael believes a knockout loss to Pavlovich could make the road back to another title opportunity much more complicated, particularly with a return to 205 pounds seemingly off the table. Chael has always believed in Pereira’s ability to win. Now, for the first time, he’s questioning what a devastating loss could mean for the former champion’s future. **Could Sergei Pavlovich deliver the knockout that changes everything for Alex Pereira?** #ChaelSonnen #AlexPereira #SergeiPavlovich #MichaelBisping #UFC #MMA #UFCHeavyweight #MMAAnalysis #UFCNews

articles.title: Chael To Shevchenko: 'What Happened? Tell Your Story'
articles.description: New DraftKings Customers turn five bucks into one hundred and fifty in total bonuses, paid over 14 days. The Crown Is Yours! Sign up using https://dkng.co/sonnen or through my promo code SONNEN. #DKPartner A week removed, and Chael still can't bring himself to call her the champion. She won the strawweight title, sure. But in his mind she didn't win the strawweight title, and she is not holding the UFC belt. He lays out why, and it starts with Valentina Shevchenko. Chael walks through the mystery that has him stuck: the word used was "vacated," which has a definition, it means she did it on purpose, like Khabib did. Except he never heard she was hurt. Never saw it on the great shows, never saw it in the threads, never saw a word on social media that she might not make the date. Then one day the vacant title is being fought for, and he's asking the questions nobody else will: was she in agreement with it? How long were these discussions going? Because if there is one thing more powerful in America than the doctor, the lawyer, the millionaire, or the producer, it is the victim. Is that what she is here? Along the way comes the most backhanded love letter he's ever given Shevchenko: the quietly unbreakable record, four title fights carried from the co-main slot, the mother who was a world champion, the sister who's a badass, the underground myth that she's a foreign spy because she's as good with weapons as without them. He hates how she tells that story. But he respects the hell out of the fighter. Chael Sonnen is produced by Bad Guy Inc. articles.title: The Real Reason Alex Pereira Lost
articles.description: New DraftKings Customers turn five bucks into one hundred and fifty in total bonuses, paid over 14 days. The Crown Is Yours! Sign up using https://dkng.co/sonnen or through my promo code SONNEN. #dkpartner Chael isn't buying the simple story everyone is telling about Alex Pereira's night against Ciryl Gane. The easy explanation is size, that Pereira was overwhelmed by a bigger man, but Chael lays out why that answer falls apart the moment you look at history. Muhammad Ali won his first heavyweight championship at 198 pounds. Mike Tyson, in his prime, weighed exactly 220 and Chael can't recall a single fight where size did Tyson's talking for him. And Pereira himself already made this exact move once, going from 185 to 205 and having an easier time of it, not a harder one. So what really happened? Chael points to something he has never seen from Gane before: a level of forward pressure and aggression that wasn't there against Jon Jones or Junior dos Santos, something that got into him that night and had him charging. From a wrestling mind, that's the real tell, because some fighters can fight going backwards and some simply can't, and Chael asks the uncomfortable question, does Pereira have a problem going backwards? He is usually the larger man, usually the taller man, usually holding the reach. This time he wasn't. That, Chael says, is a very different board than the size story, and it's the one worth watching. Chael says this is way hotter than anyone is giving it credit for, because Strickland says so much that people stop listening, and this time he meant something real. This, Chael says, is the beginning of action being taken, and it raises the one question nobody can answer yet: just how big a star is Sean Strickland? Then Chael reads the tea leaves. Strickland's pay complaint is simple math: Conor McGregor makes $30 million to fight for 30 seconds, and the UFC doesn't want to pay them a fraction of it. Strickland's answer, in his own words: go to 205, knock out the contract, and fight Jake Paul. "That sounds fun." The kicker: it's in writing. Chael walks through what happens if this lands in court with Mike Fuller, the lead MMA attorney in America, reading that tweet. And he notes the complication nobody talks about: Strickland didn't just tag another fighter. Jake Paul is not another fighter. This is the contract standoff story of the year, and it started with a tweet. articles.title: Did Jake Paul Do Sean Strickland Dirty?
articles.description: New DraftKings Customers turn five bucks into $150 in total bonuses, paid over 14 days. The Crown Is Yours! Sign up using https://dkng.co/sonnen or through my promo code SONNEN. #dkpartner Jake Paul just told the world that Sean Strickland has been texting him, and Chael Sonnen says it was the smartest move Jake could have made. Here is the problem: Jake Paul is not just a fighter, he is a promoter. Contacting a fighter who is under contract is viewed very differently from contacting a promoter, and the wrong move opens the door to someone calling the whole thing a work. So Jake went public with one simple, very legal question: "Are you still under contract?" In this clip, Chael breaks down why two guys who want to do business have to go through a third party, why making the whole thing public was probably done on legal advice, and why it lessens the chance of anyone claiming it was staged. He even scores it: after going back and forth, Chael says Jake got this right. Plus, Chael admits that if he could pick any fight for Jake Paul, Strickland is the one he would choose. articles.title: Morales Took The Bait. Now He's Stuck.
articles.description: New DraftKings Customers turn five bucks into one hundred and fifty in total bonuses, paid over 14 days. The Crown Is Yours! Sign up using https://dkng.co/sonnen or through my promo code SONNEN. #dkpartner Michael Morales, 19-0, versus Shavkat Rakhmonov, 19-0. Chael loves it as a marketing angle: identical records, a striker's ledger against a grappler's ledger. But put both undefeateds on the same card and you've cleared a massive opening for a third man. Then the Islam wrinkle: according to Islam Makhachev himself, two more fights, Morales and Rakhmonov, then he's out. Asked to pick on Team Islam's behalf, Chael takes the third man: Carlos Prates, because the event's own producer had the numbers and Prates was easily the biggest of the three fights. Chael's thesis: you can accidentally make a fight. A back-and-forth captures the public's imagination and "how do you un-fry that egg?" Morales can take the Rakhmonov bait because he's sitting on an ace: he knows he's getting Islam next. And Chael raises the stakes: "I'm going to see your 19-0 and I'm going to raise you an Amosov," ~27-1, the guy who'd take all four of them and still can't get his name in the conversation. If Rakhmonov versus Morales happens, by virtual elimination Prates is next for Islam. #MMA #UFC #Welterweight Bad Guy Inc merch now available at https://BadGuyInc.com Click here to subscribe: https://bit.ly/3FrHIPK Follow me on IG: https://bit.ly/3HY7BIE Follow me on Twitter: https://bit.ly/3tvY5J7 Follow me on Threads https://www.threads.com/@sonnench

articles.title: Is Diego Lopes a BMF?
articles.description: New DraftKings Customers turn five bucks into one hundred and fifty in total bonuses, paid over 14 days. The Crown Is Yours! Sign up using https://dkng.co/sonnen or through my promo code SONNEN. #DKPartner Chael Sonnen just drew a line the UFC will not like: Diego Lopes is not a BMF. He has fought for championships, sure, but BMF status comes with veteran status, and Lopes has not been around long enough. That caught even the room off guard. Here is Chael's thesis. The BMF belt is not supposed to be linear. It is a one-off belt, so stop worrying about passing it on to someone else (0:28). It does not have to happen once a year or once a month. Let it be super special. Let it happen only between two guys who are truly deserving. If you turn it into just another title, it means nothing, like a fake Olympic medal presented at a local tournament, same metal, no meaning (1:16). Chael likes the idea of a lineage, but admits there is nothing he can do about that now. So build it up instead. Have the media talk about it. Have Joe Rogan call some guy the next BMF, then let it happen eight months later (2:19). That is how you make it different and unique. And he points to the blueprint: Nate Diaz vs Jorge Masvidal, two guys with rough records who were never champions and never would be, and the Rock walked into Madison Square Garden and wrapped the belt around the winner's waist (3:07). That is what the BMF is supposed to be. Do not kill it by making it a regular belt. Eddie Hearn says the contract bars Dana White, Zuffa Boxing, and TKO from any promotional or production role, with written confirmation from SELA. Dana White insists the UFC is producing the entire event with his own team. Chael says geography, not lawyers, decides the outcome: if Dana steps inside the ring on fight night, Dana wins. articles.title: 'Could This BE THE END for Alex Pereira?' | Sergei Pavlovich vs Alex Pereira at UFC 335
articles.description: Michael Bisping breaks down Alex Pereira vs Sergei Pavlovich at UFC 335. Can Poatan’s knockout power put him back in heavyweight title contention, or could another defeat leave him questioning his future in the sport? Bisping discusses Pavlovich’s power, Pereira’s options at light heavyweight and whether Alex would want to rebuild as a contender. Plus, his thoughts on Charles Oliveira vs Diego Lopes for the BMF title and Joe Pyfer vs Bo Nickal. Who wins Pereira vs Pavlovich? articles.title: Dana White: Wang Cong "Is Gonna Hate Herself"
articles.description: Dana White: Wang Cong "Is Gonna Hate Herself" Dana didn't sugarcoat the UFC 332 main event at the UFC 332 post-fight press conference.
